item.description:
The first beta: Treewise browses, copies and moves like Windows Explorer, signed and notarized so it opens without a warning.
### Added - A disk image to install from: drag Treewise into Applications. Started from elsewhere, Treewise offers once to move itself there. - Updates through Sparkle: Check for Updates… in the Treewise menu, and a daily check that can be turned off in Settings. - Copying and moving by dragging onto the list, the sidebar, a tab, the path bar or empty space, with a "Move to"/"Copy to" badge that follows ⌥ and ⌘; dragging to and from Finder, and from Mail and other apps that drag promised files. - Cut, copy and paste, also through the system pasteboard; ⌥⌘V moves what ⌘C copied. New folder, inline rename and Move to Trash, all undoable. - A conflict dialog with Replace, Keep Both and Stop, and Apply to All. - A progress panel for long transfers, in bytes and naming the file being copied, with Pause, Resume and Stop, also inside a large file. - An icon view with thumbnails beside the list (⌘1 and ⌘2), Quick Look with Space, and context menus. - Keyboard shortcuts for tabs, panes, opening and searching, listed in the README; split view is ⌥⌘\. Settings has a button to System Settings, where any menu item can get a key of its own. - Settings (⌘,): hidden files, file extensions, row size, the start folder, and where a double-clicked folder opens. - The last window's panes, tabs, sort order and view come back after a restart. - The app icon. - Browsing the disk on macOS: a sidebar with Favorites and a Locations tree from This Mac, tabs per pane, split view with two panes, a sortable list (Name, Date Modified, Size, Kind), a path bar and a status bar; folders update live when their contents change. - Dutch and German, following the system language. - The core model and rules: drag move-or-copy, "copy" names for conflicts, per-tab history, tabs and split panes, sorting, and date, size and kind formatting.
